fields.v: Moumoula, M. B., Nikiema, S. L., Malloy, T., Kaboré, A. K., Klein, J., Bissyandé, T. F. (2026). A Low Similarity Score Does Not Show Independence after Source-Conditioned Repository Rewriting. arXiv:2611.07887v1 [cs.SE], 5 Nov 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2611.07887v1 [cs.SE] (ACM journal template, 'Publication date: November 2026', no venue named); no published venue stated
University of Luxembourg, Luxembourg (all six authors; academic)

Evaluates — empirical study of agent-only, source-conditioned rewriting of six copyleft Python repositories (69 rewrites) and of what token-similarity scores (JPlag) and retention signals can show about independence; RQ1 feasibility and cost, RQ2 run-to-run stability, RQ3 calibration against same-task independent controls

No SDD approach. Agent: GitHub Copilot agent mode in Visual Studio Code, default settings (version not stated). Models: Claude Haiku 4.5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5.4 mini, Qwen 3.7 Plus (controlled part); Claude, Gemini, Qwen in replication part (identifiers in replication package). Prompts: S1 layout-preserving, S2 paradigm shift, S3 ground-up rearchitecture

None prescribed by an SDD approach. Fixed prompts (rewriting, cleanup, repair) and a per-project kit: behavioural harness (5-6 executable cases), ordered test cases, repair prompt. Same-task independent controls built from a capability specification and the harness

(1) Rewriting with prompt S1/S2/S3 on a fresh working copy (operator sends only 'Continue'); (2) cleanup prompt (S3 only); (3) testing and repair in a new chat until all harness cases pass, edits restricted to integration code; (4) archiving before and after repair, checks that no original file is unchanged and no entry point imports the original
None on code: operator pastes fixed prompts and 'Continue' (median three per rewriting session), never edits code or comments on failures

JPlag 6.3.0 similarity (mean and max of directional similarities; minimum token match 12) before and after repair; joint criterion (sim < θ and pass) at θ = 15/25/30%; variance decomposition (project, agent, interaction, repetition); threshold straddling; import and fingerprint retention, margin vs unrelated originals, ΔSTIC vs same-task controls, AUC; five other detectors in appendix (copydetect, Dolos, MOSS, PMD CPD, line Jaccard)

Automatic: JPlag runs, harness execution, session logs for time and tokens, scripted fact extraction for retention. Statistics: Wilson 95% intervals, Wilcoxon signed-rank on paired scores, sum-of-squares shares, Kruskal-Wallis, AUC with 2,000 bootstrap resamples

Success criterion stated by the authors (for the study question, not as approach success): harness pass, and the joint criterion sim < 25% and pass. Quality verdict per configuration on these terms; cost: no criterion stated by the authors. RQ1 (Deep-Live-Cam, 1 run each, Copilot agent mode; similarity after repair, all pass the harness): (1) Claude Haiku 4.5: S1 64.3%, S2 50.9%, S3 8.2% (meets joint criterion only under S3). (2) DeepSeek V4 Pro: S1 65.9%, S2 78.2%, S3 22.8% (S3 meets). (3) Gemini 2.5 Pro: S1 16.3%, S2 8.1%, S3 21.8% (all meet). (4) GPT-5.4 mini: S1 62.9%, S2 45.0%, S3 75.1% (none). (5) Qwen 3.7 Plus: S1 99.5%, S2 88.0%, S3 14.7% (S3 meets). Rewriting 8-125 min (median 18), repair 5-59 min (median 15); 13.1M tokens rewriting, 20.0M repair over 15 runs. RQ2 (S3, 6 projects x 3 runs): Claude, Gemini, Qwen; overall 46/54 pass (Gemini 18/18; 8 failures are Claude and Qwen, 6 on ChatTTS), 42/54 below 25%, 34/54 meet joint criterion; median 12.6%; 338M tokens / 33.1 h rewriting, 217M / 39.4 h repair. Per-agent RQ2 values only in figure/appendix

Tasks: 6 copyleft Python projects (Deep-Live-Cam for RQ1). Configurations: 5 models x 3 prompts on one project (1 run each) and 3 models x 6 projects x 3 repetitions with S3. Baselines/references: five unrelated originals, and one same-task independent control per project (written by one author; must pass harness and score 0% JPlag). Held constant: agent tool (Copilot agent mode, default settings), fixed prompts, single operator, fresh working copy, harness. Acceptance tests: fixed behavioural harness per project. Repetitions: 1 (RQ1), 3 (RQ2/RQ3). Human intervention: operator only pastes prompts and 'Continue'

Prompt: median similarity 64% (S1), 51% (S2), 22% (S3), ordering holds for 3 of 5 agents; one run per cell, so no comparison between prompts or agents is supported. Stability: repetition explains 61% of variance, project 14%, project x agent 25%, agent 0.1%; no detectable project or agent effect (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.23, 0.33); 7 of 18 configurations straddle 25%. Repair: no systematic direction (Wilcoxon p = 0.74). Retention: rewrites keep 53.6% imports and 47.7% fingerprint vs 9.8%/12.7% for unrelated originals, but controls retain as much (atomic 49.7% vs 44.5%); AUC 0.40 (0.15-0.67) and 0.45 (0.28-0.65), intervals include 0.5

It showed that repeated runs dominate variation and that single scores cannot separate rewrites from independent code. Authors' stated limits: RQ1 one run per cell; three repetitions make the variance decomposition descriptive; AUC on six negatives with wide intervals; controls one per project, written by one author who knew the originals, extended after first results; RQ3 is a sensitivity result, not a planned test

Construct: token similarity is surface correspondence; harness covers 5-6 cases (20-58% of lines); cost only time and tokens, no money; fingerprint corpus-dependent. Internal: agent edits in place, leftover original files; repair went beyond integration changes on Algo; single operator; possible training-data recall; model updates. Conclusion: small repetitions, RQ1 one run, six negatives. External: six Python projects < 15,000 SLOC, mostly ML applications, one agent tool, five models, three prompts, same language, no specification-only runs. Future work: spec-only agent runs, several controls per project, held-out inputs and differential testing, other languages and larger repositories

Appendix with per-run RQ2 figures, coverage and other detectors is referenced but not in the text read. Duplicate sentence on operator effects in threats (p. 16). Claims to release the 69 rewrites, harnesses and scores and a replication package with model identifiers, but no URL given in the text. No pre-registration.
